hero.title: Spiks Ride-Hailing
hero.subtitle: A university-focused ride coordination platform designed for fast matching, visibility, and route-aware dispatching.

origin.pullQuote: Campus mobility is a systems problem, not just a map problem.
paragraphs: Spiks was initiated to improve informal transport coordination in a constrained campus environment where latency, route uncertainty, and pickup ambiguity directly affect user trust.
The product direction prioritized lightweight client interactions and location-aware backend matching to ensure riders and drivers could converge quickly with minimal operational overhead.

architecture.title: Real-Time Dispatch and Geo-Indexing Layers
architecture.description: A TypeScript-first application with geospatial indexing and request-to-driver matching flows.
architecture.narrative: The system combines request intake, geo-filtering, and matching logic into a low-latency flow. Driver availability and rider proximity are treated as first-class constraints. The architecture is designed to remain robust under small bursts of concurrent requests while preserving predictable matching behavior and minimizing rider wait uncertainty.

hardParts.title: Reducing Dispatch Conflicts Under Concurrent Requests
hardParts.description: Preventing double assignment and stale availability state was the most critical challenge.
hardParts.narrative: When multiple rider requests targeted the same nearby drivers, race conditions caused conflicting assignments. The mitigation introduced reservation semantics during allocation, plus post-allocation verification to reject stale states. This significantly improved dispatch integrity and reduced user-visible inconsistencies.
